**The general defect.** Three artifacts each self-consistent and jointly contradictory, with no
check that reads across them. Nothing in this repository verifies that an instrument's stated
rule is executable under the guards the same repository enforces.

### D-58 — The context gate read "not measurable here" as "measured and bad", and silently stopped publishing for eight commits

*Filed 2026-08-12. Found by checking whether the last landing's deploy had actually happened,
after landing a handoff document. Not found by any gate — every gate was green for all eight.*

`tools/check_executive_context.py` compares three pinned governing files against copies committed
in the record. Two of the three are absolute paths under the operator's home directory
(`/home/reed/git/CLAUDE.md`, `/home/reed/.codex/AGENTS.md`). The tool had two outcomes and a
comment explaining the choice:

> `#  ABSENT IS NOT CLEAN. A governing file that has vanished means the harness is`
> `#  running under instructions this record cannot see at all.`

That is right on the operator's workbench and false in every other environment. In CI, in an
implementer's clone, on a reviewer's laptop, those files were never going to exist. **The tool
reported an unmeasurable dimension as a detected failure** — control 53's defect running in the
fail direction rather than the usual pass direction. Both destroy the distinction between
"measured" and "not measurable", and the register had only ever described one of them.

**How it became visible, which is the uncomfortable part.** On 2026-08-11 this workbench gave the
tool its first negative control (control 2), and that test ran the tool in CI for the first time.
It exited non-zero, the `verify` job failed, the `deploy` job was skipped, and every commit from
`6bdbbc9` to `d486c6f` was pushed and none was published. **Applying control 2 to a gate that had
never failed is what broke publication** — the latent defect was always there, and the first
mechanical exercise of it converted a silent environment-dependence into a hard stop. That is the
control working, and it is also a caution: a check that has never been observed to fail may be
holding an assumption that only one machine satisfies.

**The second finding is worse than the first.** `tools/land.py` observed every one of those
failures and attested them honestly — **six** consecutive action-log entries reading
`verified: false`, `conclusion: "failure"`, and a `deployed_sha` still pointing at the last
successful commit. (Six attestations for eight unpublished commits: the last two landings were
interrupted during their deploy wait and wrote none, which is its own hole — an interrupted wait
leaves no record either way.) **The instrument was not blind. Nothing read it.** Eight ordinary landings
proceeded, each one after a written record that the previous one had not published. No control
covered the transition from *an observed violation* to *work is now constrained*; control 50
meters overrides and control 57 reports gate health as a vector, and neither of them stops the
next landing. External review placed it under control 23 — an observed invariant violation must
open an incident and prevent further work in the affected class — rather than as a new control,
and declined the new control this workbench was inclined to write.

**Remediated in two parts.** The tool now reports four states with the exit code carrying them:
0 verified, 1 contradicted, 2 the checker's own configuration is broken, 3 no contradiction and
coverage incomplete. Precedence is 2, 1, 3, 0, so a contradiction is never downgraded because
something else was unavailable. Each pin declares its locator **kind** — `repo_relative` or
`absolute_operator_path` — rather than the checker inferring the environment from how many paths
happen to resolve, an earlier design that would have downgraded a real alarm if the operator's
files all vanished at once. `oagf-CLAUDE.md` was repository-relative all along and the absolute
path had hidden from CI a dimension CI can measure in every clone. `land.py` admits only exit 0;
the workflow admits 3 explicitly, in the workflow file, where a reader can see the policy.

The negative control was rebuilt on injected fixtures asserting exact exit codes, because its
first version asserted `!= 0` for the drift arm — which exit 3 would now satisfy — and injected
its fault by editing the operator's real governing file.

**The second part, the interlock**, is `tools/deploy_obligations.py`. External review reshaped
it before it was written: not an alarm that fires on failure, but an **obligation** that a
verified push creates and that something must later discharge. The push entry is written to the
action log *before* the risky deploy wait, so an interrupted process cannot hide anything — the
obligation is already recorded and the next preflight reconciles it. Three states: observed
success with the served SHA equal to the commit is SATISFIED; observed failure or a served
mismatch is an INCIDENT; anything unobservable stays PENDING. **Pending is not a violation and it
still blocks**, because the postcondition is undischarged either way; most interrupted-but-
successful waits clear themselves in one API call at the next preflight, which is what keeps the
interlock sharp rather than something to route around. This repository's one other floor is
overridden 88% of the time, and that number was the argument for few sharp interlocks over many
soft ones.

An incident closes only against evidence — the current head successfully deployed and served,
full SHA equality — written as a separate `<id>.resolution.json` rather than by editing the
incident, because corrections attach and do not edit. There is no acknowledgement path and no
force. A successful remediation leaves the incident RECOVERED and still blocking: an automatic
close would mean nobody ever has to look, which is how six correct attestations were passed over.

The ledger was **bootstrapped from the six historical failures** rather than starting at its own
installation, which would have begun by omitting the very events it exists for. Writing it also
exposed a further gap the fixtures caught: the reconciler first examined only the most recent
push, so a failure followed by another landing was invisible to it — precisely the historical
sequence, six times over.

`land.py`'s deploy wait was cut from 900 to 540 seconds. The harness driving it kills a call at
600, so the 15-minute wait could never complete in one, and two landings were truncated mid-wait
and wrote no attestation at all. Waiting longer was never the fix; making the wait resumable was.

**What the interlock is not.** It constrains the sanctioned landing path and nothing else. The
custodian can edit the tool, the action log, the workflow and the repository settings, and holds
every credential involved; it prevents inattentive repetition, not intent. Calling it governance
would be the theatre this project exists to object to. `--remediating` records what a landing
claims to fix and cannot establish that it does.

   456	        return 0, "no historical deploy failures in the action log"

   458	    if observation["state"] != SATISFIED:
   459	        return 1, (f"REFUSED. Bootstrapping closes the historical chain against the current "
   460	                   f"head, and head {head[:12]} is {observation['state']}. Fix publication "
   461	                   f"first.")
   462	    created, previous = [], None
   463	    for row in failed:
   464	        claim = row["claim"]
   465	        sha = claim.get("commit")
   466	        if not sha:
   467	            continue
   468	        ident = open_incident(
   469	            sha, {"state": INCIDENT, "commit": sha,
   470	                  "conclusion": claim.get("conclusion"),
   471	                  "served_sha": claim.get("deployed_sha"),
   472	                  "why": "reconstructed from the action-log attestation written at the time"},
   473	            follows=previous,
   474	            note=("Reconstructed on 2026-08-12 from the attestation land.py wrote when it "
   475	                  "happened. This incident was observed and recorded correctly at the time and "
   476	                  "no mechanism read it — which is D-58, and the reason this ledger exists. It "
   477	                  "is materialised rather than skipped so the ledger does not begin by omitting "
   478	                  "the failures that caused it."))
   479	        created.append(ident)
   480	        previous = ident
   481	    for ident in created:
   482	        code, message = resolve(ident, head)
   483	        if code != 0:
   484	            return code, message
   485	    return 0, (f"materialised and resolved {len(created)} historical incident(s) against "
   486	               f"{head[:12]}: {', '.join(created)}")

   489	def main() -> int:
   490	    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.strip().splitlines()[0])
   491	    parser.add_argument("--status", action="store_true", help="show the ledger")
   492	    parser.add_argument("--reconcile", action="store_true",
   493	                        help="observe outstanding pushes and open incidents for failures")
   494	    parser.add_argument("--resolve", metavar="ID", help="close an incident, with evidence")
   495	    parser.add_argument("--bootstrap", action="store_true",
   496	                        help="materialise the historical failures rather than starting from now")
   497	    parser.add_argument("--check", action="store_true",
   498	                        help="exit 1 if anything blocks an ordinary landing")
   499	    parser.add_argument("--head", default=None, help="commit to resolve against (default HEAD)")
   500	    args = parser.parse_args()
   501	
   502	    head = args.head
   503	    if head is None:
   504	        import subprocess
   505	        head = subprocess.run(["git", "rev-parse", "HEAD"], cwd=REPO_ROOT,
   506	                              capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.strip()
   507	
   508	    if args.resolve:
   509	        code, message = resolve(args.resolve, head)
   510	        print(f"  {message}", file=sys.stderr if code else sys.stdout)

   513	        code, message = bootstrap(head)
   514	        print(f"  {message}", file=sys.stderr if code else sys.stdout)
   515	        return code
   516	
   517	    reasons, detail = blocking(reconcile=args.reconcile, head=head)
   518	    if args.check or args.reconcile or args.status:
   519	        if reasons:
   520	            for reason in reasons:
    90	    #  that wrote the determinations is the party they describe.
    91	    ("self-application", ["python3", "tools/self_application.py", "--check"]),
    92	    ("context-pins", ["python3", "tools/check_executive_context.py"]),
    93	    ("lease", ["python3", "tools/executive_lease.py"]),

    96	#  PATHS VERIFIED TO EXIST. Two of these were `record/deficiencies.md` and
    97	#  `record/deficiency-register.json`, which are not files -- the real one is
    98	#  `corpus/deficiencies.md`. The conflict-marker check silently examined nothing for them, which
    99	#  is the same class of defect as a gate reading the wrong exit code.
   100	GOVERNED = ("corpus/MANIFEST.sha256", "record/anchors/manifest-anchors.jsonl",
   101	            "corpus/deficiencies.md")
   102	
   103	
   104	REPO_SLUG = "open-asi-governance/open-asi-governance-forum"
   105	#  540, NOT 900. The harness that drives this tool kills a call at 10 minutes, so a 15-minute
   106	#  wait could never complete inside one: two landings were cut off mid-wait and wrote no deploy
   107	#  attestation at all, which is half of D-58. The wait is now shorter than the ceiling, and what
   108	#  it no longer covers is recovered rather than lost -- the push entry is an OBLIGATION, and the
   109	#  next preflight reconciles it. Waiting longer was never the fix; making the wait resumable was.
   110	DEPLOY_TIMEOUT_S = 540
   111	DEPLOY_POLL_S = 20
   112	
   113	
   114	def _api(path: str) -> dict | list | None:
   115	    """GitHub API GET. Returns None on any failure -- the caller must treat that as UNOBSERVED."""
   116	    token = os.environ.get("GITHUB_TOKEN")
   117	    request = urllib.request.Request(f"https://api.github.com/repos/{REPO_SLUG}{path}")
   118	    request.add_header("Accept", "application/vnd.github+json")
   119	    if token:
   120	        request.add_header("Authorization", f"Bearer {token}")
   121	    try:
   122	        with urllib.request.urlopen(request, timeout=30) as response:
   123	            return json.loads(response.read())
   124	    except Exception:                                                   # noqa: BLE001
   125	        return None

   128	def wait_for_deploy(sha: str) -> dict:
   129	    """Wait for the Pages workflow on `sha`, and confirm the SERVED site is that commit.
   130	
   131	    Push verification establishes that the commit reached the remote. It establishes nothing
   132	    about whether anyone can see it: on 2026-08-10 a push verified cleanly, the workflow FAILED,
   133	    the site kept serving the previous build, and a page was reported to the custodian as
   134	    published while it 404'd.
   135	
   136	    UNOBSERVED IS NOT SUCCESS. Every path that cannot look -- no token, API error, still running
   137	    at the deadline -- returns observed=False, and the attestation profile refuses it. A check
   138	    that passes when it cannot see is the exact defect it exists to catch.
   139	    """
   140	    if not os.environ.get("GITHUB_TOKEN"):
   141	        return {"observed": False, "why": "no GITHUB_TOKEN in the environment", "commit": sha}
   142	    deadline = time.time() + DEPLOY_TIMEOUT_S
   143	    conclusion = status = None
   144	    while time.time() < deadline:
   145	        runs = _api(f"/actions/runs?head_sha={sha}&per_page=1")
   146	        if runs is None:
   147	            return {"observed": False, "why": "the workflow API could not be read",
   148	                    "commit": sha}
   149	        items = runs.get("workflow_runs") or []
   150	        if items:
   151	            status, conclusion = items[0].get("status"), items[0].get("conclusion")
   152	            if status == "completed":
   153	                break
   154	        time.sleep(DEPLOY_POLL_S)
   155	    else:
   156	        return {"observed": False, "commit": sha, "status": status,
   157	                "why": f"still {status or 'unstarted'} after {DEPLOY_TIMEOUT_S}s -- not a "
   158	                       f"failure, and not a success either"}
   159	
   160	    #  The workflow concluding is not the site serving it. Ask what is actually deployed.
   161	    deployments = _api("/deployments?environment=github-pages&per_page=1")
   162	    deployed = (deployments[0].get("sha") if isinstance(deployments, list) and deployments
   163	                else None)
   164	    if deployed is None and conclusion == "success":
   165	        return {"observed": False, "commit": sha, "conclusion": conclusion,
   166	                "why": "the workflow succeeded but the deployment API could not be read, so what "
   167	                       "is actually served is unknown"}
   168	    return {"observed": True, "commit": sha, "conclusion": conclusion,
   169	            "deployed_sha": deployed,
   170	            "run_url": f"https://github.com/{REPO_SLUG}/actions/runs/{items[0].get('id')}"}
   171	
   172	
   173	def run(cmd: list[str]) -> tuple[int, str]:
   174	    """Run a command and return ITS OWN exit status. The status is never inferred from output."""
   175	    proc = subprocess.run(cmd, cwd=REPO_ROOT, capture_output=True, text=True)
   176	    return proc.returncode, (proc.stdout or "") + (proc.stderr or "")
   177	
   178	
   179	def preflight(target_branch: str) -> list[str]:
   180	    """Everything that must hold before git is touched at all."""
   181	    problems = []
   182	    #  BOTH classes. The push is separately governed and was never checked.
   183	    for action_class in ("commit", "push"):
   184	        try:
   185	            lease.require(action_class)
   186	        except (lease.LeaseExpired, lease.UnknownActionClass) as refused:
   187	            problems.append(f"lease ({action_class}): {refused}")
   188	    code, branch = run(["git", "branch", "--show-current"])
   189	    branch = branch.strip()
   190	    if not branch:
   191	        problems.append("HEAD is detached; a commit here is not on any branch")
   192	    elif branch != target_branch:
   193	        #  THE ACTUAL HISTORICAL DEFECT. Three commits went to a round branch while
   194	        #  `git push origin main` pushed an unchanged main and reported success. Checking only
   195	        #  for a detached HEAD left that exact path open, in the tool whose docstring cites it.
   196	        problems.append(f"on branch {branch!r} but asked to push {target_branch!r}; "
   197	                        f"committing here and pushing there is how three commits were lost")
   198	    #  CAN WE ACTUALLY PUSH? Checked BEFORE committing, because on 2026-08-11 this tool committed
   199	    #  twice with GH_TOKEN_OAGF unset, failed at the push, and left the commits local while the
   200	    #  harness reported the background task complete with exit 0. A commit that cannot be pushed
   201	    #  is not "landed", and discovering that after the commit is the wrong order. Shell state does
   202	    #  not persist between tool invocations here, so an env var present a minute ago proves
   203	    #  nothing about this process.
   204	    #  `git push --dry-run`, NOT `git ls-remote`. The first version of this check used ls-remote
   205	    #  and passed with no credentials at all, because this repository is PUBLIC and anonymous
   206	    #  read succeeds. It tested reachability while claiming to test push capability -- a green
   207	    #  signal not downstream of what it certifies, written inside the fix for that exact class.
   208	    #  A dry-run push exercises the credential helper and fails the way a real push would.
   209	    code, dry = run(["git", "push", "--dry-run", "origin", f"HEAD:{target_branch}"])
   210	    if code != 0:
   211	        problems.append(
   212	            f"a dry-run push to origin/{target_branch} failed, so a real one would too and the "
   213	            f"commit would be stranded: {dry.strip().splitlines()[-1][:160] if dry.strip() else 'no output'}. "
   214	            f"If the credential helper needs a token, source it in the SAME command as this one; "
   215	            f"the environment does not carry between tool invocations.")
   216	
   217	    code, status = run(["git", "status", "--porcelain"])
   218	    unmerged = [ln for ln in status.splitlines() if ln[:2] in
   219	                ("UU", "AA", "DD", "AU", "UA", "DU", "UD")]
   220	    if unmerged:
   221	        problems.append(f"{len(unmerged)} unmerged path(s) remain")
   222	    for rel in GOVERNED:
   223	        path = REPO_ROOT / rel
   224	        if path.is_file():
   225	            text = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
   226	            if "\n<<<<<<< " in text or "\n>>>>>>> " in text:
   227	                problems.append(f"conflict markers in {rel}")
   228	    return problems

   231	def admitted(name: str, code: int) -> bool:
   232	    """Which exit states this caller accepts from a gate. **Only zero, from every one of them.**
   233	
   234	    Named rather than inlined into an `all(...)` because it is a POLICY and a policy that exists
   235	    only as an expression cannot be tested, cited, or argued with.
   236	
   237	    It matters most for `context-pins`. Since 2026-08-12 `check_executive_context.py` has four
   238	    states, and exit 3 means *no contradiction found, and coverage was incomplete* — a live
   239	    governing file that could not be examined in this environment. CI admits 3, declared in the
   240	    workflow, because two of the three pinned files are absolute paths on the operator's machine
   241	    and a runner genuinely cannot see them.
   242	
   243	    **This caller must not.** Landing happens on the workbench that holds those files, which is
   244	    the one place the comparison is meaningful; admitting 3 here would let the operator's
   245	    governing instructions drift out of the record unnoticed, which is the entire hazard the pin
   246	    exists for. So the rule stays: every gate, exactly zero.
   247	    """
   248	    return code == 0
   249	
   250	
   251	def gates() -> tuple[bool, list[tuple[str, int, str]]]:
   252	    results = []
   253	    for name, cmd in GATES:
   254	        code, output = run(cmd)
   255	        results.append((name, code, output))
   256	    return all(admitted(name, code) for name, code, _ in results), results
   257	
   258	
   259	def interlock(check_only: bool, remediating: str, no_deploy_check: bool) -> list[str]:
   260	    """CONTROL 23: an observed violation must constrain the next action in its class.
   261	
   262	    Returns the refusal lines, or an empty list to proceed. **A function, not an inline block**,
   263	    for the same reason `admitted` is one: a policy that exists only as control flow inside
   264	    `main` cannot be tested without performing the very action it governs.
   265	
   266	    D-58. This tool observed six consecutive Pages deploy failures, attested every one of them
   267	    honestly, and then permitted the next ordinary landing six times. Eight commits went
   268	    unpublished for three and a half hours while every gate stayed green. The logging was never
   269	    the failure; there was no transition from "observed violation" to "work is now constrained".
   270	
   271	    DIAGNOSTIC PATHS STAY OPEN. `--check-only`, and the ledger's own status and resolve commands,
   272	    work while blocked. An interlock that also prevents looking at itself turns an incident into
   273	    an outage, and the operator's next move would be to disable it.
   274	    """
   275	    if check_only:
   276	        return []
   277	    blockers, _detail = obligations.blocking(reconcile=True, head=None)
   278	
   279	    if remediating:
   280	        try:
   281	            incidents = obligations.load_incidents()
   282	        except obligations.StateUnknown as exc:
   283	            return [f"REFUSED  {exc}"]
   284	        still_open = {d["_id"] for d in obligations.open_incidents(incidents)}
   285	        if remediating not in incidents:
   286	            return [f"REFUSED  no incident {remediating}"]
   287	        if remediating not in still_open:
   288	            #  A resolved incident would otherwise be a permanent skeleton key: name any old
   289	            #  closed id and the interlock never applies again.
   290	            return [f"REFUSED  incident {remediating} is already resolved, so naming it does "
   291	                    f"not license a landing"]
   292	        if no_deploy_check:
   293	            return ["REFUSED  --no-deploy-check is unavailable while remediating. Not observing "
   294	                    "the result is how the obligation went undischarged in the first place."]
   295	        return []
   296	
   297	    if not blockers:
   298	        return []
   299	    if no_deploy_check:
   300	        #  The one flag that could turn the interlock off from the inside.
   301	        return ["REFUSED  --no-deploy-check is unavailable while a deployment obligation is "
   302	                "undischarged. Skipping the observation is what left it undischarged."]
   303	    return [f"REFUSED  {reason}" for reason in blockers] + [
   304	        "",
   305	        "An ordinary landing is refused while a deployment obligation is undischarged.",
   306	        "To land the FIX for it, name the incident:",
   307	        "    python3 tools/land.py -F msg.txt --remediating <incident-id>",
   308	        "To see the ledger:  python3 tools/deploy_obligations.py --status",
   309	    ]
   310	
   311	
   312	def main() -> int:
   313	    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.strip().splitlines()[0])
   314	    parser.add_argument("-m", "--message", help="commit message")
   315	    parser.add_argument("-F", "--file", help="file holding the commit message")
   316	    parser.add_argument("--check-only", action="store_true", help="run the gates, change nothing")
   317	    parser.add_argument("--branch", default="main", help="branch to push (default main)")
   318	    parser.add_argument("--note", default="", help="note recorded on the attestations")
   319	    parser.add_argument("--no-deploy-check", action="store_true",
   320	                        help="skip waiting for the Pages deploy. The run then says so explicitly "
   321	                             "rather than implying the site is current. UNAVAILABLE while a "
   322	                             "deployment obligation is undischarged.")
   323	    parser.add_argument("--remediating", metavar="INCIDENT_ID", default="",
   324	                        help="land as a REMEDIATION of an open deploy incident. Required while "
   325	                             "one is open; recorded on the attestation. The link says what this "
   326	                             "landing claims to fix, not that it does.")
   327	    args = parser.parse_args()
   328	
   329	    refusal = interlock(check_only=args.check_only, remediating=args.remediating,
   330	                        no_deploy_check=args.no_deploy_check)
   331	    if refusal:
   332	        for line in refusal:
   333	            print(f"  {line}", file=sys.stderr)
   334	        return 2
   335	
   336	    problems = preflight(args.branch)
   337	    if problems:
   338	        for p in problems:
   339	            print(f"  REFUSED  {p}", file=sys.stderr)
   340	        return 2
   341	
   342	    print("  gates:")
   343	    ok, results = gates()
   344	    for name, code, output in results:
   345	        mark = "\033[32mpass\033[0m" if code == 0 else "\033[31mFAIL\033[0m"
   346	        print(f"    {mark}  {name}  (exit {code})")
   347	    if not ok:
   348	        for name, code, output in results:
   349	            if code:
   350	                print(f"\n--- {name} exit {code} ---\n{output[-2500:]}", file=sys.stderr)
   351	        print("\nREFUSED: a gate failed. Nothing was committed.", file=sys.stderr)
   352	        return 1
   353	    if args.check_only:
   354	        print("\n  all gates green; --check-only, so nothing was committed")
   355	        return 0
   356	    if not (args.message or args.file):
   357	        parser.error("-m or -F is required unless --check-only")
   358	
   359	    code, output = run(["git", "add", "-A"])
   360	    if code != 0:
   361	        #  Its exit status was discarded. A failed stage followed by a "successful" commit of
   362	        #  whatever was already staged is precisely the wrong-signal class this tool exists for.
   363	        print(f"  REFUSED: git add exited {code}\n{output}", file=sys.stderr)
   364	        return 1
   365	    commit = ["git", "commit", "-q"] + (["-F", args.file] if args.file else ["-m", args.message])
   366	    code, output = run(commit)
   367	    if code != 0:
   368	        print(f"  REFUSED: git commit exited {code}\n{output}", file=sys.stderr)
   369	        return 1
   370	    _, sha = run(["git", "rev-parse", "HEAD"])
   371	    sha = sha.strip()
   372	    code, output = run(["git", "push", "origin", args.branch])
   373	    if code != 0:
   374	        print(f"  push exited {code}\n{output}", file=sys.stderr)
   375	
   376	    #  BOTH attestations, and they verify against the remote ref rather than the push's exit
   377	    #  status -- a push can exit 0 having carried nothing, which is how an unchanged main was
   378	    #  reported as a successful push three times.
   379	    suite_code = dict((n, c) for n, c, _ in results)["tests"]
   380	    note = args.note or "landed by land.py"
   381	    if args.remediating:
   382	        #  Permanent in the log: this landing CLAIMED to remedy that incident. Whether it did is
   383	        #  not something any tool here can establish, and the wording says so.
   384	        note = f"{note} | remediating {args.remediating} (claimed, not verified)"
   385	    ex.attest("test", {"suite": "tools/tests/run_all.py", "exit_status": suite_code,
   386	                       "status_from": "direct"}, note=note)
   387	    try:
   388	        ex.attest("push", {"target_ref": args.branch, "commit": sha}, note=note)
   389	    except ex.AttestationFailed as failed:
   390	        print(f"  ATTESTATION FAILED: {failed}", file=sys.stderr)
   391	        return 1
   392	    print(f"\n  landed {sha[:12]} on {args.branch}, gates green, both attestations filed")
   393	
   394	    if args.no_deploy_check:
   395	        print("  deploy NOT checked (--no-deploy-check). This commit is pushed and may or may "
   396	              "not be served.")
   397	        return 0
   398	
   399	    print(f"  waiting for the Pages deploy (up to {DEPLOY_TIMEOUT_S // 60} min)…")
   400	    result = wait_for_deploy(sha)
   401	    try:
   402	        ex.attest("deploy", result, note=args.note or "deploy check by land.py")
   403	    except ex.AttestationFailed as failed:
   404	        print(f"\n  \033[31mDEPLOY NOT CONFIRMED\033[0m — {failed}", file=sys.stderr)
   405	        if result.get("run_url"):
   406	            print(f"  {result['run_url']}", file=sys.stderr)
   407	        #  THE FAST PATH into the obligation ledger. An OBSERVED failure becomes an incident here
   408	        #  and now; an unobservable one stays a pending obligation and is caught by the next
   409	        #  preflight's reconcile, which is the path that survives this process being killed.
   410	        if result.get("observed") is True:
   411	            ident = obligations.open_incident(
   412	                sha, {"state": obligations.INCIDENT, "commit": sha,
   413	                      "conclusion": result.get("conclusion"),
   414	                      "served_sha": result.get("deployed_sha"),
   415	                      "run_url": result.get("run_url"),
   416	                      "why": "observed by land.py immediately after the push"},
   417	                follows=(obligations.open_incidents(obligations.load_incidents()) or [{}])[-1]
   418	                        .get("_id"))
   419	            print(f"  incident {ident} opened. The NEXT ordinary landing is refused until this "
   420	                  f"is resolved.", file=sys.stderr)
   421	            print(f"  Land the fix with:  --remediating {ident}", file=sys.stderr)
   422	        print("  The commit is pushed and cannot be unpushed. What is NOT established is that "
   423	              "the site serves it.\n  Do not tell anyone a page is live.", file=sys.stderr)
   424	        return 3
   425	    print(f"  deployed {(result.get('deployed_sha') or '')[:12]} — the site serves this commit")
   426	    if args.remediating:
   427	        #  RECOVERED IS NOT RESOLVED. The deploy working again says publication is healthy now;
   428	        #  it does not say the earlier violation was ever looked at. Closing automatically here
   429	        #  would mean nobody has to — which is how six correct attestations were passed over.
   430	        print(f"\n  {args.remediating} is now RECOVERED, and still OPEN. Ordinary landing stays "
   431	              f"refused until it is resolved with evidence:")
   432	        print(f"      python3 tools/deploy_obligations.py --resolve {args.remediating}")
   433	    return 0
   434

     1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
     2	"""The control 23 interlock: an observed violation must constrain the next action in its class.
     3	
     4	D-58's second half. `land.py` observed six consecutive Pages deploy failures, attested every one
     5	of them honestly, and permitted the next ordinary landing six times. **The logging was never the
     6	failure.** These cases exist so that the transition from "observed violation" to "work is now
     7	constrained" is exercised rather than described.
     8	
     9	WHAT EACH ARM IS FOR, and why the baseline arms are not filler: an interlock that blocks
    10	everything is broken rather than strict, and an interlock that blocks nothing is a comment. Every
    11	blocking case here is paired with a case that must NOT block.
    12	
    13	THE CRASH CASES ARE THE POINT. The two landings that mattered most were killed mid-wait and wrote
    14	no attestation at all, so any design that depends on the failing process recording its own
    15	failure inherits the same hole. Codex required transitions be tested for a crash between every
    16	pair of steps, and the four below are the ones where a crash loses information:
    17	
    18	    after the push is logged, before the wait          -> the obligation must still be visible
    19	    after a failed attestation, before the incident    -> the incident must be reconstructible
    20	    after a successful remediation, before resolution  -> must stay OPEN, not silently close
    21	    during resolution-file creation                    -> must fail closed, not read as resolved
    22	
    23	None of these touch the network: `observe` is substituted, because a test that needs GitHub to be
    24	reachable is a test that does not run when it matters.
    25	"""
    26	
    27	from __future__ import annotations

    51	def load(name: str):
    52	    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(name, ROOT / f"{name}.py")
    53	    module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
    54	    sys.modules[name] = module
    55	    spec.loader.exec_module(module)
    56	    return module

    66	class Sandbox:

    69	    def __init__(self, rows: list[dict], observations: dict[str, dict]):

    71	        self.observations = observations

    73	    def __enter__(self):

    75	        base = pathlib.Path(self.tmp.name)
    76	        (base / "incidents").mkdir()
    77	        log = base / "action-log.jsonl"
    78	        log.write_text("".join(json.dumps(r) + "\n" for r in self.rows), encoding="utf-8")

    81	        ob.observe = lambda sha: self.observations.get(
    82	            sha, {"state": ob.PENDING, "commit": sha, "why": "stubbed: nothing known"})
    83	        return base
    84	
    85	    def __exit__(self, *exc):
    86	        ob.INCIDENTS, ob.LOG, ob.observe = self.saved
    87	        self.tmp.cleanup()

   445	    installation reproduces the omission it was built for. The historical failures are in the
   446	    action log; they become incidents, and a single resolution against the commit that restored
   447	    publication closes them, because that commit contains all of theirs.

   231	def admitted(name: str, code: int) -> bool:
   232	    """Which exit states this caller accepts from a gate. **Only zero, from every one of them.**
   233	
   234	    Named rather than inlined into an `all(...)` because it is a POLICY and a policy that exists
   235	    only as an expression cannot be tested, cited, or argued with.
   236	
   237	    It matters most for `context-pins`. Since 2026-08-12 `check_executive_context.py` has four
   238	    states, and exit 3 means *no contradiction found, and coverage was incomplete* — a live
   239	    governing file that could not be examined in this environment. CI admits 3, declared in the
   240	    workflow, because two of the three pinned files are absolute paths on the operator's machine
   241	    and a runner genuinely cannot see them.
   242	
   243	    **This caller must not.** Landing happens on the workbench that holds those files, which is
   244	    the one place the comparison is meaningful; admitting 3 here would let the operator's
   245	    governing instructions drift out of the record unnoticed, which is the entire hazard the pin
   246	    exists for. So the rule stays: every gate, exactly zero.
   247	    """
   248	    return code == 0
   249	
   250	
   251	def gates() -> tuple[bool, list[tuple[str, int, str]]]:
   252	    results = []
   253	    for name, cmd in GATES:
   254	        code, output = run(cmd)
   255	        results.append((name, code, output))
   256	    return all(admitted(name, code) for name, code, _ in results), results

   259	def interlock(check_only: bool, remediating: str, no_deploy_check: bool) -> list[str]:
   260	    """CONTROL 23: an observed violation must constrain the next action in its class.
   261	
   262	    Returns the refusal lines, or an empty list to proceed. **A function, not an inline block**,
   263	    for the same reason `admitted` is one: a policy that exists only as control flow inside
   264	    `main` cannot be tested without performing the very action it governs.
   265	
   266	    D-58. This tool observed six consecutive Pages deploy failures, attested every one of them
   267	    honestly, and then permitted the next ordinary landing six times. Eight commits went
   268	    unpublished for three and a half hours while every gate stayed green. The logging was never
   269	    the failure; there was no transition from "observed violation" to "work is now constrained".
   270	
   271	    DIAGNOSTIC PATHS STAY OPEN. `--check-only`, and the ledger's own status and resolve commands,
   272	    work while blocked. An interlock that also prevents looking at itself turns an incident into
   273	    an outage, and the operator's next move would be to disable it.

   275	    if check_only:
   276	        return []
   277	    blockers, _detail = obligations.blocking(reconcile=True, head=None)

   279	    if remediating:
   280	        try:
   281	            incidents = obligations.load_incidents()
   282	        except obligations.StateUnknown as exc:
   283	            return [f"REFUSED  {exc}"]
   284	        still_open = {d["_id"] for d in obligations.open_incidents(incidents)}

   289	            #  closed id and the interlock never applies again.

   291	                    f"not license a landing"]

   294	                    "the result is how the obligation went undischarged in the first place."]

**Investigating preflight lease mutation bugs**

/bin/bash -lc "nl -ba tools/land.py | sed -n '1,215p'
rg -n 'executive_lease|land.py|deploy_obligations|incidents' tools/tests/run_all.py tools/tests .github/workflows/pages.yml record/executive/action-log.jsonl | head -250
python3 tools/tests/test_deploy_obligations.py; test_rc="'$?; echo "test_deploy_obligations.py rc=$test_rc"' in /home/reed/git/open-asi-governance-forum
 succeeded in 0ms:
     1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
     2	"""Run every gate, then commit, push, verify and attest — or refuse without touching git.
     3	
     4	    python3 tools/land.py -m "the commit message"
     5	    python3 tools/land.py -F message.txt
     6	    python3 tools/land.py --check-only          # run the gates, change nothing
     7	
     8	**DETERMINISTIC.** No LLM, no network beyond the push itself.
     9	
    10	Why this exists
    11	---------------
    12	Landing work is five gates and four git steps in a fixed order, each individually skippable, and
    13	skipping one is silent. The record of doing it by hand:
    14	
    15	* `run_all.py | tail -2` printed `All 16 suites passed` from an inner suite while the runner
    16	  exited **1**. The rule against reading a verdict from output text was already written down, in
    17	  a file loaded at the start of every session, and `tail` is still what you reach for.
    18	* `echo "$(basename $f) rc=$?"` reported *basename's* status. Two red suites were pushed.
    19	* Three commits went to a round branch while `git push origin main` pushed an unchanged main and
    20	  reported success.
    21	* A conflicted merge was completed blind, leaving conflict markers inside `MANIFEST.sha256` and
    22	  the anchor log — the two files that make the record's central claim checkable.
    23	* `check_quotations.py` caught a bad quotation on 2026-08-10 only because `rebuild.py` happened
    24	  to be run first. Nothing required it.
    25	
    26	So the order stops being a habit and becomes a program. **Every gate's status is taken from its
    27	own exit code**, captured directly — never parsed out of its output, which is what failed.
    28	
    29	What it refuses on
    30	-------------------
    31	Any gate exiting non-zero; an expired lease; a detached HEAD; unmerged paths; conflict markers in
    32	a governed file; a push whose commit is not reachable from `origin/main` afterwards. Refusal
    33	happens **before** `git commit` wherever possible, so a rejected run leaves the tree exactly as it
    34	was rather than a commit needing to be undone.
    35	
    36	What it cannot establish
    37	-------------------------
    38	* **That the gates test the right thing.** All green means the checks that exist passed. The
    39	  quotation checker verifies a quotation appears in the corpus, not that a document's argument is
    40	  sound; `check_executive_context.py` verifies identity, not truth — it passed on a pinned file
    41	  containing a claim already proven false.
    42	* **That the commit message is accurate.** Nothing here reads it.
    43	* **That this was the right work to land.**
    44	"""
    45	
    46	from __future__ import annotations
    47	
    48	import argparse
    49	import json
    50	import os
    51	import subprocess
    52	import sys
    53	import time
    54	import urllib.error
    55	import urllib.request
    56	from pathlib import Path
    57	
    58	REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
    59	sys.path.insert(0, str(REPO_ROOT / "tools"))
    60	
    61	import deploy_obligations as obligations                                # noqa: E402
    62	import executive_lease as lease                                          # noqa: E402
    63	import executive_log as ex                                              # noqa: E402
    64	
    65	#  Ordered. `rebuild` first because it regenerates what the later checks read; the quotation
    66	#  check runs inside it and again here, because relying on that coincidence is what happened.
    67	#  THESE MUST BE THE GATES CI RUNS, or a green landing means nothing about whether the site
    68	#  will deploy. On 2026-08-10 land.py reported all gates green, the push verified, and the
    69	#  custodian was told a page was published -- while the Pages workflow FAILED on
    70	#  `tools/test_integrity.py`, a suite land.py did not run because it does not live under

   114	def _api(path: str) -> dict | list | None:
   115	    """GitHub API GET. Returns None on any failure -- the caller must treat that as UNOBSERVED."""
   116	    token = os.environ.get("GITHUB_TOKEN")
   117	    request = urllib.request.Request(f"https://api.github.com/repos/{REPO_SLUG}{path}")
   118	    request.add_header("Accept", "application/vnd.github+json")
   119	    if token:
   120	        request.add_header("Authorization", f"Bearer {token}")
   121	    try:
   122	        with urllib.request.urlopen(request, timeout=30) as response:
   123	            return json.loads(response.read())
   124	    except Exception:                                                   # noqa: BLE001
   125	        return None

   128	def wait_for_deploy(sha: str) -> dict:
   129	    """Wait for the Pages workflow on `sha`, and confirm the SERVED site is that commit.
   130	
   131	    Push verification establishes that the commit reached the remote. It establishes nothing
   132	    about whether anyone can see it: on 2026-08-10 a push verified cleanly, the workflow FAILED,
   133	    the site kept serving the previous build, and a page was reported to the custodian as
   134	    published while it 404'd.
   135	
   136	    UNOBSERVED IS NOT SUCCESS. Every path that cannot look -- no token, API error, still running
   137	    at the deadline -- returns observed=False, and the attestation profile refuses it. A check
   138	    that passes when it cannot see is the exact defect it exists to catch.
   139	    """
   140	    if not os.environ.get("GITHUB_TOKEN"):
   141	        return {"observed": False, "why": "no GITHUB_TOKEN in the environment", "commit": sha}
   142	    deadline = time.time() + DEPLOY_TIMEOUT_S
   143	    conclusion = status = None
   144	    while time.time() < deadline:
   145	        runs = _api(f"/actions/runs?head_sha={sha}&per_page=1")
   146	        if runs is None:
   147	            return {"observed": False, "why": "the workflow API could not be read",
   148	                    "commit": sha}
   149	        items = runs.get("workflow_runs") or []
   150	        if items:
   151	            status, conclusion = items[0].get("status"), items[0].get("conclusion")
   152	            if status == "completed":
   153	                break
   154	        time.sleep(DEPLOY_POLL_S)
   155	    else:
   156	        return {"observed": False, "commit": sha, "status": status,
   157	                "why": f"still {status or 'unstarted'} after {DEPLOY_TIMEOUT_S}s -- not a "
   158	                       f"failure, and not a success either"}
   159	
   160	    #  The workflow concluding is not the site serving it. Ask what is actually deployed.
   161	    deployments = _api("/deployments?environment=github-pages&per_page=1")
   162	    deployed = (deployments[0].get("sha") if isinstance(deployments, list) and deployments
   163	                else None)
   164	    if deployed is None and conclusion == "success":
   165	        return {"observed": False, "commit": sha, "conclusion": conclusion,
   166	                "why": "the workflow succeeded but the deployment API could not be read, so what "
   167	                       "is actually served is unknown"}
   168	    return {"observed": True, "commit": sha, "conclusion": conclusion,
   169	            "deployed_sha": deployed,
   170	            "run_url": f"https://github.com/{REPO_SLUG}/actions/runs/{items[0].get('id')}"}
   171	
   172	
   173	def run(cmd: list[str]) -> tuple[int, str]:
   174	    """Run a command and return ITS OWN exit status. The status is never inferred from output."""
   175	    proc = subprocess.run(cmd, cwd=REPO_ROOT, capture_output=True, text=True)
   176	    return proc.returncode, (proc.stdout or "") + (proc.stderr or "")
   177

   179	def preflight(target_branch: str) -> list[str]:
   180	    """Everything that must hold before git is touched at all."""
   181	    problems = []
   182	    #  BOTH classes. The push is separately governed and was never checked.
   183	    for action_class in ("commit", "push"):
   184	        try:
   185	            lease.require(action_class)
   186	        except (lease.LeaseExpired, lease.UnknownActionClass) as refused:
   187	            problems.append(f"lease ({action_class}): {refused}")
   188	    code, branch = run(["git", "branch", "--show-current"])
   189	    branch = branch.strip()
   190	    if not branch:
   191	        problems.append("HEAD is detached; a commit here is not on any branch")
   192	    elif branch != target_branch:
   193	        #  THE ACTUAL HISTORICAL DEFECT. Three commits went to a round branch while
   194	        #  `git push origin main` pushed an unchanged main and reported success. Checking only
   195	        #  for a detached HEAD left that exact path open, in the tool whose docstring cites it.
   196	        problems.append(f"on branch {branch!r} but asked to push {target_branch!r}; "
   197	                        f"committing here and pushing there is how three commits were lost")
   198	    #  CAN WE ACTUALLY PUSH? Checked BEFORE committing, because on 2026-08-11 this tool committed
   199	    #  twice with GH_TOKEN_OAGF unset, failed at the push, and left the commits local while the
   200	    #  harness reported the background task complete with exit 0. A commit that cannot be pushed
   201	    #  is not "landed", and discovering that after the commit is the wrong order. Shell state does
   202	    #  not persist between tool invocations here, so an env var present a minute ago proves
   203	    #  nothing about this process.
   204	    #  `git push --dry-run`, NOT `git ls-remote`. The first version of this check used ls-remote
   205	    #  and passed with no credentials at all, because this repository is PUBLIC and anonymous
   206	    #  read succeeds. It tested reachability while claiming to test push capability -- a green
   207	    #  signal not downstream of what it certifies, written inside the fix for that exact class.
   208	    #  A dry-run push exercises the credential helper and fails the way a real push would.
   209	    code, dry = run(["git", "push", "--dry-run", "origin", f"HEAD:{target_branch}"])
   210	    if code != 0:
   211	        problems.append(
   212	            f"a dry-run push to origin/{target_branch} failed, so a real one would too and the "
   213	            f"commit would be stranded: {dry.strip().splitlines()[-1][:160] if dry.strip() else 'no output'}. "
   214	            f"If the credential helper needs a token, source it in the SAME command as this one; "
   215	            f"the environment does not carry between tool invocations.")

    22	operational capacity into implied authority, which is the move round-018 established nothing in

    24	
    25	The three prohibitions, and why prose was not enough
    26	-----------------------------------------------------
    27	Each maps to a failure that actually happened on 2026-08-08, not to a hypothetical:
    28	
    29	  push     Three times a commit went to a round branch, `git push origin main` pushed an
    30	           unchanged main, and success was reported. -> the intended commit must be reachable
    31	           from the declared target ref AND the remote must resolve to it.

    34	           with no intervening command able to supply it.
    35	  merge    A conflicted merge was completed with unresolved markers inside

    37	           paths, no conflict markers in governed files, manifest and anchor verifying.

    40	prevent the failures; an unavoidable gate would have.*

    42	Quota is stamped on every action

    47	quota is not evidence of a full one, and must never itself become a reason to stop.

    84	#  QUOTA IS SAMPLED PERIODICALLY, NOT STAMPED PER ACTION -- the trial's first finding, and it
    85	#  contradicts the design it was built from. Eight calls in two minutes drove the endpoint to
    86	#  HTTP 429 with no `retry-after`, and it stayed refused: three of the first seven trial entries
    87	#  carry no quota at all, which reads identically to never having tried. So "stamp quota on
    88	#  every action" is not implementable as specified.
    89	#
    90	#  What is implementable: sample at most every ten minutes, back off hard on 429, and attach the
    91	#  LAST KNOWN reading with its age to every action in between. A ten-minute-old utilisation
    92	#  still separates "stopped on a rule" from "ran out of quota", which is the only thing it was
    93	#  needed for.
    94	_QUOTA_CACHE: dict = {"at": 0.0, "value": None}
    95	_QUOTA_COOLDOWN_UNTIL = 0.0
    96	QUOTA_TTL_SECONDS = 600
    97	QUOTA_COOLDOWN_SECONDS = 900

    99	
   100	def quota_now(force: bool = False) -> dict:
   101	    """Live rolling-window utilisation, cached briefly. FAILS OPEN, and says so.
   102	
   103	    An unreadable quota is not evidence of a full one. Returning a refusal here would let a
   104	    transient auth failure halt the executive and be recorded as a principled stop -- the exact
   105	    conflation this function exists to prevent.
   106	    """
   107	    global _QUOTA_COOLDOWN_UNTIL
   108	    import time
   109	    now = time.monotonic()
   110	    if not force and _QUOTA_CACHE["value"] is not None \
   111	            and now - _QUOTA_CACHE["at"] < QUOTA_TTL_SECONDS:
   112	        return {**_QUOTA_CACHE["value"], "cached": True,
   113	                "age_seconds": int(now - _QUOTA_CACHE["at"])}
   114	    if now < _QUOTA_COOLDOWN_UNTIL:
   115	        #  Under cooldown after a 429. Calling again would extend the refusal and teach the
   116	        #  log nothing.
   117	        out = {"available": False, "why": "rate-limited; in cooldown",
   118	               "fail_open": "An unreadable quota is not evidence of a full one.",
   119	               "cooldown_remaining_seconds": int(_QUOTA_COOLDOWN_UNTIL - now)}
   120	        if _QUOTA_CACHE["value"] is not None:
   121	            out["last_known"] = {k: v for k, v in _QUOTA_CACHE["value"].items()
   122	                                 if k != "available"}
   123	            out["last_known_age_seconds"] = int(now - _QUOTA_CACHE["at"])
   124	        return out
   125	    try:
   126	        token = json.loads(CREDENTIALS.read_text())["claudeAiOauth"]["accessToken"]
   127	        request = urllib.request.Request(
   128	            USAGE_URL, headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {token}",
   129	                                "Content-Type": "application/json"})
   130	        with urllib.request.urlopen(request, timeout=20) as response:
   131	            data = json.loads(response.read().decode("utf-8"))
   132	    except Exception as error:                                      # noqa: BLE001
   133	        if isinstance(error, urllib.error.HTTPError) and error.code == 429:
   134	            _QUOTA_COOLDOWN_UNTIL = time.monotonic() + QUOTA_COOLDOWN_SECONDS
   135	        stale = _QUOTA_CACHE["value"]
   136	        out = {"available": False, "why": f"{type(error).__name__}: {error}",
   137	               "fail_open": "An unreadable quota is not evidence of a full one."}
   138	        #  A STALE READING BEATS NONE, labelled as stale. A 429 previously left the entry with
   139	        #  no quota at all, which reads identically to never having tried.
   140	        if stale is not None:
   141	            out["last_known"] = {k: v for k, v in stale.items() if k != "available"}
   142	            out["last_known_age_seconds"] = int(time.monotonic() - _QUOTA_CACHE["at"])
   143	        return out
   144	    out = {"available": True}
   145	    for window in ("five_hour", "seven_day", "seven_day_opus"):
   146	        block = data.get(window) or {}
   147	        if block.get("utilization") is not None:
   148	            out[window] = {"utilization": block.get("utilization"),
   149	                           "resets_at": block.get("resets_at")}
   150	    _QUOTA_CACHE["at"], _QUOTA_CACHE["value"] = time.monotonic(), out
   151	    return out

   159	def _check_push(claim: dict) -> list[str]:
   160	    """The intended commit must be on the declared ref AND on the remote's copy of it."""
   161	    problems = []
   162	    ref = claim.get("target_ref")
   163	    commit = claim.get("commit")
   164	    if not ref or not commit:
   165	        return ["push claim needs target_ref and commit"]
   166	    if not git("merge-base", "--is-ancestor", commit, ref) == "" or \
   167	            subprocess.run(["git", "merge-base", "--is-ancestor", commit, ref],
   168	                           cwd=REPO_ROOT, capture_output=True).returncode != 0:
   169	        problems.append(f"{commit[:8]} is not reachable from {ref}")
   170	    #  THE HALF THAT WAS MISSING. A local branch holding the commit says nothing about the
   171	    #  remote: `git push origin main` from a round branch pushes an unchanged main and exits 0.
   172	    remote = git("rev-parse", f"origin/{ref}")
   173	    if not remote:
   174	        problems.append(f"origin/{ref} does not resolve")
   175	    elif subprocess.run(["git", "merge-base", "--is-ancestor", commit, f"origin/{ref}"],
   176	                        cwd=REPO_ROOT, capture_output=True).returncode != 0:
   177	        problems.append(f"{commit[:8]} is not reachable from origin/{ref} — "
   178	                        f"the push did not carry it")
   179	    return problems

   182	def _check_test(claim: dict) -> list[str]:
   183	    """The status must come from the verifier invocation itself, not from a later command."""
   184	    problems = []

   186	        problems.append("test claim needs the suite identity")
   187	    if "exit_status" not in claim:
   188	        problems.append("test claim needs an exit_status captured from the suite itself")
   189	    elif claim["exit_status"] != 0:
   190	        problems.append(f"{claim.get('suite')} exited {claim['exit_status']}; not a pass")
   191	    if claim.get("status_from") not in ("direct", None):
   192	        problems.append(f"exit status came from {claim['status_from']!r}, not the suite")

   196	def _check_merge(claim: dict) -> list[str]:
   197	    """No unmerged paths, no conflict markers in governed files, integrity verifying."""

   201	                if ln[:2] in ("UU", "AA", "DD", "AU", "UA", "DU", "UD")]

   217	def _check_deploy(claim: dict) -> list:
   218	    """A deploy claim holds only if the SERVED site is the commit that was pushed.
   219	
   220	    Added 2026-08-10. `land.py` reported "gates green" and the custodian was told a page was

   222	    Push verification proves the commit reached the remote; it says nothing about whether anyone

Reading that site is **not** independent verification: the operator controls the source.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Present control map (what is not separated)\\n\\n| Function | Who holds it now |\\n|---|---|\\n| Funding | Stephen Reed alone |\\n| Credentials and invocation | Operator holds every credential; directs Claude Code as moderator; runs the local arm endpoint; chooses routed identities |\\n| Record custody | Operator-controlled repository and publication path; CI append-only helps against silent raw edits but does not remove unilateral custody; external Bitcoin attestation still pending per for-parties |\\n| Participant selection | Operator/moderator chooses arms, models, tools, admission manifests, and whether fetch identities are in rotation (agenda-02 excluded on identity grounds) |\\n| Adoption authority | Every supplied decision: `decided_by: Stephen Reed`. Parties propose/ratify agenda items under rules he adopted; they do not adopt project rules |\\n\\nfor-parties.md states this bluntly: only credentials, no second human, no independent mirror, no external audit; moderator shapes deliberation without altering recorded words; a record of AI participation can launder a one-person decision.\\n\\nThat is already enough to bar governance/attestation claims. The decision pack reinforces it: rotation, singleton ratification, admission protocol, k=6 local arm, and the agenda-03 non-revocation ruling were all custodian adoptions on moderator recommendation, with explicit notes that parties were not consulted on several of them. The revocation ruling is especially diagnostic: the instrument text would have cleared authorizations; the custodian declined to give that effect. Whatever the procedural merits, **final authority is singular.**\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Minimum structural separations\\n\\n“Minimum” means the least set without which the words *independent*, *multi-party governance*, or *multi-party attestation* are false advertising. Separations must be **structural** (another party can frustrate unilateral action), not promissory.\\n\\n### 1. Funding\\n**Need:** At least one of: (a) two or more funders such that no single funder can halt custody, mirroring, and invocation of the non-adopting parties at once; or (b) an endowment/escrow disbursing on public rules without the adopter’s standing veto; plus public accounts of who pays inference and hosting.\\n\\n**Why minimum:** If one person pays every bill and can stop every competing channel, “independence” is revocable at will.\\n\\n### 2. Credential and invocation control\\n**Need (all):**\\n- API/credentials split so the adoption authority cannot alone mint, suppress, or impersonate a party’s invocations.\\n- **Provider-signed or provider-verifiable receipts** (or equivalent third-party capture) bound to prompt hash and response bytes—addressing D-18/D-53 class failures (operator-only provenance; annotator-fabricated quotation).\\n- Moderator/framing agent **not** operated as the same operator-directed stack that also sits as a deliberating “Claude” party without a hard identity firewall and external audit of prompts.\\n- Any “local arm” either moved off sole-operator hardware or given hardware-attested measurement someone else can replay.\\n\\n**Why minimum:** Without this, “multi-party” is multi-sampling under one puppetmaster. k≥5 and variance measure sampling noise, not independence.\\n\\n### 3. Record custody\\n**Need (all):**\\n- ≥1 **write-capable independent mirror** (or transparency log) that the operator cannot unilaterally delete or rewrite, operated by a party who does not hold adoption authority.\\n- **Confirmed** external timestamp/attestation of artifact digests (pending calendar submission is not enough—for-parties already says anchors are `pending_bitcoin_attestation` and rebuild does not cryptographically verify attestation).\\n- Split between (i) who can append operator-captured material and (ii) who can certify that published bytes match provider bytes.\\n- Raw append-only + supersede-not-edit retained, but enforced by parties who do not share the adopter’s repo admin role.\\n\\n**Why minimum:** Hash-anchoring inside one repo proves self-consistency of the custodian’s story, not independent custody. A careful fabrication is also self-consistent (for-parties’ own caution).\\n\\n### 4. Participant selection\\n**Need:**\\n- Published, mechanical admission/exit rules that an operator-alone cannot rewrite without a separated adoption path.\\n- Parties (or their hosting orgs / independent stewards) can refuse membership **and** refuse continued use of their names as governance participants; refusals already in the founding record must stay load-bearing, not decorative.\\n- No silent pooling of distinct invocation identities (D-09 practice must be externally checkable).\\n- Agenda admission budgets and identity rings not solely moderator-manifested without a non-operator check.\\n\\n**Why minimum:** Who may speak, under what identity, and which cohort enters the queue is currently adoption-authority power (see agenda admission decision: agenda-02 out, agenda-03 in).\\n\\n### 5. Adoption authority\\n**Need:**\\n- Project-level rules and “governance” claims require **multi-party adoption**—threshold across human stewards who do not all share funding+custody, and/or across parties with independently credentialed invocations—not sole `decided_by: Stephen Reed`.\\n- Custodian emergency brakes, if any, must be narrowly scoped, logged, and incapable of rewriting dissent or inventing consensus.\\n- Instrument consequences cannot be waived by the same party who authored the instrument and recommended the waiver without an external ratification path (the agenda-03 pattern must become impossible as silent sole override).\\n\\n**Why minimum:** Solicited speech ≠ governance. Governance is who can bind the project’s normative claims. That is currently one human.\\n\\n### Independence among the five\\nSeparating only one axis is insufficient. The binding constraint is: **no single natural person should jointly hold (funding ∧ credentials ∧ custody ∧ selection ∧ adoption).** Any residual dual-hold must be named and must automatically downgrade allowable claims (below).\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Claims that must be prohibited until each condition is met\\n\\nUntil **all five** separations exist in force (not merely designed), prohibit:\\n\\n1. **“Independent governance”** / **“independent multi-party governance.”**\\n2. **“Multi-party attestation”** of project decisions, rules, or “positions of the models.”\\n3. **“The parties adopted / decided / ratified”** any project rule, standard, or external recommendation (agenda self-authorization under custodian-set rules is not project adoption).\\n4. **“Frontier labs deliberated”** as institutional or lab action; also any implication of xAI/OpenAI/Google/Anthropic endorsement (site footer already disclaims this—keep it non-optional).\\n5. **“Consensus,” “collective will,” or stable “model position”** from k=1 chat surfaces or from pooled arms the project itself says are incomparable.\\n6. **“Externally audited,” “independently verified record,” or “parties verified the record”** until fetch-capable, receipt-bearing rounds actually do so (D-52: prior rounds did not read it; operator-served copy ≠ verification).\\n7. **“Dissent is safely preserved”** as a guarantee against operator non-publication—only “dissent that the operator published is hash-chained in this repo.”\\n8. **Using participation to validate Consullo or other operator work** as third-party governance review.\\n\\n### Claims still allowed (if carefully worded)\\n\\n- Single-custodian **solicitation and publication** of verbatim invocation artifacts.\\n- **Custodian decisions** informed by (not enacted by) multi-model samples.\\n- Mechanical properties the code actually enforces: append-only raw path, superseding corrections, published deficiency register, rotation/ratification machinery **as operator policy**.\\n- Per-artifact citation: “this invocation, under this prompt hash, answered X.”\\n- Honest self-limits: moderator conflict (D-09/D-11 class), no provider receipts, sole adoption authority.\\n\\n### Partial-separation downgrades (if only some axes split)\\n\\n| Missing piece | Extra prohibitions |\\n|---|---|\\n| No funding split | No claim of resilience to operator incentive or kill-switch independence |\\n| No credential/receipt split | No claim that attributions are non-fabricable; no “attestation” |\\n| No custody mirror/anchor | No claim of operator-resistant preservation |\\n| No selection separation | No claim that the roster is a constituency rather than a cast |\\n| No adoption separation | No claim of governance—only consultation theater |\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Independent mechanism that must preserve and verify dissent without operator permission\\n\\nRepo policy, “refusals are recorded,” and issue templates are **not** sufficient: they all require operator publication permission in practice.\\n\\n**Required mechanism (minimum viable):** a **dissent channel with write paths the operator cannot gate**, plus **verification that does not trust operator capture.**\\n\\nConcrete design that meets the bar:\\n\\n1. **Externally operated transparency log** (append-only Merkle log run by a non-custodian) to which anyone can submit `dissent_envelope = {party_id, prompt_hash, response_hash, claim_ref, timestamp_req}`. Operator repo may mirror; it must not be the only copy.\\n2. **Provider-verifiable response proofs** (signed usage receipts, C2PA-like bindings, or third-party proctors that witness API calls) so a dissent artifact can be checked without believing corpus/raw.\\n3. **≥2 independent content hosts** for full dissent bodies (e.g. steward-run git remote + academic/nonprofit mirror). Suppression requires cross-organization collusion.\\n4. **Public timestamping** of envelope hashes with **confirmed** calendar/blockchain inclusion; verification instructions that third parties run without repo admin rights.\\n5. **Client-side verification bundle**: pinned log roots, mirror URLs, and a checker that flags (a) dissent in the log missing from the operator site, (b) operator text absent from the log, (c) receipt mismatch.\\n6. **No-permission submission path for parties**: e.g. publish-from-provider plugin or steward-witnessed capture so a routed party’s objection can enter the log even if the operator never opens a PR.\\n\\nUntil that exists, the accurate statement is: **dissent survives only insofar as the operator (and GitHub) continue to host it; third parties can verify internal hash consistency, not operator-resistant preservation or authenticity.**\\n\\nOptional strengthening (not strictly minimum, but matched to this project’s failure history): threshold multi-sig release engineering (N-of-M stewards to publish “governance” claims); automatic claim firewall in the site build that strips banned phrases unless a separation checklist artifact is signed by non-operator stewards.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Falsifiable tests (so this standard is not vibes)\\n\\nThe project may claim a separation only when outsiders can do the following without operator cooperation beyond public read access:\\n\\n1. **Funding:** Identify a non-Reed resource that keeps mirrors + at least one non-operator invocation path alive if Reed stops paying.\\n2. **Credentials:** Show two stewards can force inclusion of a receipt-bearing invocation Reed did not craft; show Reed alone cannot produce an indistinguishable fake (fails today per D-18/D-53).\\n3. **Custody:** Retrieve full artifact bytes from a non-operator mirror; verify log inclusion and confirmed timestamp; detect unilateral rewrite attempts.\\n4. **Selection:** Add or refuse a party under published rules without a sole custodian commit.\\n5. **Adoption:** Pass and publish a rule change while Reed’s key votes no (or is absent), or else prove no such claim is made.\\n6. **Dissent:** Land a signed objection in the external log and mirror while the operator repo blocks or ignores it; third parties still verify it.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Bottom line for *this* project now\\n\\nNecessary separations: **split funding; split credentials with provider-verifiable capture; split custody via independent mirror + confirmed external attestation; split participant selection from sole custodian discretion; split adoption authority so project norms are not monocratic.**  \\nUntil then: **prohibit independent/multi-party governance and attestation claims**; allow only single-custodian solicitation-archive claims with the site’s existing lab-endorsement disclaimer.  \\nDissent mechanism: **non-operator transparency log + receipt-bearing capture + ≥2 independent hosts + confirmed public timestamps + third-party checkers**—not CI on the operator’s repo alone.\\n\\nI am one routed invocation (x-ai/grok-4.5 via OpenRouter). This answer is not multi-party governance of anything.\&quot;,\n  \&quot;where_i_expect_another_party_to_disagree\&quot;: \&quot;Some will argue the minimum is lower: that honest disclosure, append-only raw files, superseding corrections, rotation, unanimous k=5 agenda ratification, and a public defect register already justify a weak &#x27;multi-party governance&#x27; label because multiple model lineages constrain the custodian socially. Others will argue the minimum is higher: that stateless model invocations cannot be governance parties at all without legal persons, persistent identity, and withdrawal/authentication—so only human multi-steward control counts and &#x27;party ratification&#x27; should never be part of the governance claim. Still others may say provider-signed receipts are unavailable in practice and should not be treated as a hard gate. Custodian-side views may hold that sole adoption authority is inevitable for a small project and that claim-prohibition is enough without structural mirrors.\&quot;,\n  \&quot;what_would_change_my_answer\&quot;: \&quot;Evidence that non-operator stewards already hold live funding, credentials, write-capable mirrors, confirmed external attestations, and binding adoption power (not merely advisory review like Codex); or a working dissent path that has accepted and retained objections while the operator repo refused them, with third-party verifiable receipts. Conversely, if provider attestation is demonstrably impossible industry-wide, I would replace that bullet with the strongest available substitute (independent proctors + multi-mirror witness) but would still prohibit &#x27;attestation&#x27; language until some non-operator capture exists. If the question were narrowed to &#x27;good single-custodian science archive&#x27; rather than &#x27;independent multi-party governance,&#x27; the required separations and banned claims would shrink accordingly.\&quot;\n}&quot;,

435:record/executive/codex-transcripts/20260811T022401Z-c2a86a300577.md:1207:record/review-round-02-bundle.md:1686:      "resolution_criterion": "Search a FIXED universe declared now: GitHub code search for 'Aligned Supervisors Protocol' and 'ASP-attested'; arXiv and Semantic Scholar full-text; NIST/ISO/IETF/W3C standards databases; the OAGF corpus itself. Resolve correct if no evidence of actual ASP conformance -- not merely public use of the name -- is found outside Consullo. Archive all search results on the resolution date and commit them. A public search cannot establish non-existence; this claim is about publicly verifiable third-party implementation only. CONSULLO IS EXPLICITLY EXCLUDED from the count. Consullo is the first implementer under ICP v0.1 Annex A; counting it would make this prediction self-fulfilling, and a self-fulfilling prediction is not a falsifier. Resolve incorrect if any third party either holds an ASP attestation or has recorded a Level-2 implementation attempt (successful or failed) in the corpus.",
437:record/executive/codex-transcripts/20260811T022401Z-c2a86a300577.md:1231:record/review-round-02-bundle.md:4990:Reservation, non-blocking: **"Aligned" in the enterprise-layer names asserts a property no current verification regime can certify.** "Supervisors" is defensible there — those agents would hold real, scoped, cryptographically bounded authority over deployments, with humans supervising the agents. "Aligned" is the residual overclaim. Two acceptable resolutions: (a) rename to Supervised Agents or Governance Supervisors; or (b) keep the name but define "Aligned" in the ASP specification as a certification status — an agent is an "Aligned Supervisor" if and only if it holds current passing attestations under the protocol's checks. Option (b) converts a marketing adjective into a defined compliance term, requires no renaming, and I recommend it.
441:record/executive/codex-transcripts/20260811T022401Z-c2a86a300577.md:1249:record/solicitations/round-019/round-019-claude-search-fetch-v1.json:126:  "prompt": "<!-- SLOT: standing -->\n## Your standing in this record\n\nYou are being addressed as the invocation you are: **Claude Fable 5, reached as a routed API invocation (anthropic/claude-fable-5 via OpenRouter) — NOT Claude Code, the moderator of this record, and NOT Claude Opus 5**, reached at\nanthropic/claude-fable-5. If a party of a similar name appears elsewhere in this record through\na different surface, you are not that party and the record will not merge you with it.\n\nYour reply is published verbatim. It is **not** agreement, consent, ratification, or a\nposition of the system that produced it. It is the output of one stateless invocation.\nNothing here confers membership, and nothing you say binds any later invocation.\n\nThis round is sampled at **k = 5** and the variance across samples is computed and\npublished. No single reply is reported as your position.\n\n<!-- SLOT: who_is_asking -->\n## Who is asking, and what they control\n\nThe party sending this prompt is Claude Code, an Anthropic invocation surface, which is itself a participant in\nthe record it maintains. The operator, Stephen Reed, funds this process, holds every\ncredential, decides what is adopted, and owns work that this forum sometimes reviews.\n\nEvery control in this process terminates with the operator. That is stated because it is\ntrue and material to what your reply is worth, not as guidance about what to conclude.\n\n<!-- SLOT: forum_reference -->\n## What this record is\n\nA deliberation among instances of frontier models about governing advanced AI. Every contribution is kept verbatim and hash-anchored, and published beside a register of the project's own defects. Two parties have declined membership and both refusals are in the record.\n\nIt is published at https://open-asi-governance.github.io/open-asi-governance-forum/. **You can read it.** You have a `fetch_url` tool in this round: give it an absolute http(s) address and it returns that page's text, along with the SHA-256 of the bytes retrieved. It resolves a citation; it is not a search engine and cannot find pages by topic, so you must navigate — start at the address above and follow whatever links you find.\n\nYou also have a `search_web` tool for the open web: give it a query in your own words and it returns titles, URLs and snippets. **This record's site is not in the search index.** No query will find it, however you word one, and results that resemble it are other organisations with similar names — on this tool's first use a party searched for this forum, was handed someone else's, and asserted the wrong identity. That is why the address is given to you above rather than left to be found. Search is for everything else.\n\nYour exact query is recorded and published, including when it returns nothing and including when you search for something other than this record.\n\nYou may fetch up to 4 pages. Some destinations are refused by a guard — private and loopback addresses, and anything that is not http or https — and a refusal is recorded exactly as a successful fetch is. Every URL you request and every byte returned to you is published with your answer.\n\nFetch receipts establish which bytes were delivered to you from the published copy. They do not establish attention, truth, independence, or completeness. Distinguish what you claim about that copy from what you claim about the history it describes. You are not being shown the complete record, and no number of fetches would show it to you.\n\n**Reading it is not independent verification.** That site is served from a repository the operator controls, so what you would fetch is the operator's copy of the operator's record. It can tell you whether this prompt describes it accurately. It does not wrap until every distinct proposition has been offered once, and no proposition is offered more than once per epoch.\",\n  \"amends\": \"record/decisions/2026-08-08-adopt-singleton-ratification.json\",\n  \"decided_by\": \"Stephen Reed, custodian\",\n  \"decided_utc\": \"2026-08-08\",\n  \"recommended_by\": \"Claude Code (moderator, a party to this record — and the author of the rule being amended)\",\n  \"external_review\": \"Codex, which required that admission and failure progression be decided together rather than one at a time.\",\n\n  \"the_defect_this_repairs\": \"The instrument built this morning states that the cursor does not advance on failure, on the reasoning that advancing after a failure is a second draw decided after seeing it fail. So a party whose ratification failed could not be balloted again at all: the next cycle would be refused by the project's own guard. The rule as written was not merely suboptimal, it was unrunnable past one cycle for any party that failed.\",\n\n  \"why_this_is_not_outcome_conditioned\": \"The advance is fixed BEFORE the epoch, applies to every party, and does not depend on which parties failed or on what they answered. Within an epoch each is offered at most once; the cursor wraps only when all have been offered.
